name: swift-extras-json (ExtrasJSON, formerly pure-swift-json)
baseline: Foundation JSONEncoder / JSONDecoder in Swift 5.1 and 5.2 (macOS: pre-2023 NSJSONSerialization-backed; Linux: swift-corelibs-foundation before Swift 5.5)
verdict_reason: The ~2x macOS and 7-10x Linux gains were measured in 2020 against Foundation versions that no longer ship. The author upstreamed the same value-type parsing approach into swift-corelibs-foundation in 2021, Apple platforms moved to the Swift rewrite in 2023, and nobody has compared the two since.
tier_reason: The PerfTests package is in the repo, run with swift run -c release, and the README states the 2019 Intel Core i9 MacBook Pro and Swift 5.1/5.2.
claimed_speedup: Encoding: ~2x on macOS (1.23s vs 2.61s, Swift 5.1), ~10x on Linux (1.05s vs 12.52s, Swift 5.2). Decoding: ~1.5x on macOS (1.70s vs 2.72s, Swift 5.1), ~7x-~8x on Linux (1.16s vs 10.65s, Swift 5.2).
workload: Encoding and decoding a sample Codable structure (PerfTests SampleStructure) in a loop; total seconds
hardware: 2019 MacBook Pro 16-inch, 2.4 GHz 8-core Intel Core i9
one_liner: Foundation-free JSON coder that beat Swift 5.1/5.2 Foundation by 1.5-10x; its parsing approach later went into Foundation itself.
how_it_is_fast: It parses into a Swift enum value tree instead of NSDictionary, NSArray and NSNumber reference types, avoiding Objective-C bridging and per-node reference counting, and it never touches Foundation. Encoding writes bytes directly into a [UInt8] buffer.
use_it_when: Foundation-free targets on old toolchains (Linux before Swift 5.5)
skip_it_when: Swift 5.5+ on Linux or any current Apple OS: Foundation now parses into value types too
You need Date or Data strategies, snake_case key conversion, or UTF-16/UTF-32 input: none are supported
caveats: Numbers are from 2020, Swift 5.1/5.2, on an Intel Mac.

Both baselines have since been replaced: swift-corelibs-foundation merged the author's JSONValue-based parser and coders (PRs #2966, #2985, #2987, March 2021), and macOS 14 / iOS 17 ship the Swift rewrite of JSONDecoder.
A reviewer's measurement on corelibs PR #2966 showed that change alone cut a JSONSerialization parse loop from 1.71 s to 0.67 s on Linux.
tradeoffs: No Date/Data strategies or key conversion

evidence.quote: All tests have been run on a 2019 MacBook Pro (16" – 2,4 GHz 8-Core Intel Core i9).
|  | macOS Swift 5.1 | macOS Swift 5.2 | Linux Swift 5.1 | Linux Swift 5.2 |
It should significantly improve overall JSON performance, since we save on a lot of roundtrips through NSArray and NSDictionary.
this is the last step to make JSON Encoding and Decoding much more performant on Linux.
